No lib/letflow/engine/ file is touched, matching REQ-150's own constraint and the design's own §6 claim.

four_questions.idiomatic_vs_crutch: N/A directly (no code exists yet), but the proposed module design is sound: to_lua/1 and from_lua/1 are stated as explicit identity functions for the numeric/nil cases rather than omitting numeric handling, which is the correct way to codify 'do not add coercion' as an assertable contract instead of an implicit gap. No case-do-the-state-machine's-job pattern or other crutch shape appears.
four_questions.supervision: N/A — the design proposes no process, GenServer, or gen_statem change of any kind. No isolation concern.
four_questions.type_safety_gaps: to_lua/1 and from_lua/1 are typed term() -> term() rather than a narrower union. This is a reasonable design-stage choice (one call site regardless of value shape, per §3) and the doc is explicit that non-numeric behavior is out of this rule's scope, not silently assumed identity-safe. Not filed as a type-safety issue: there is no implementation yet to make unrepresentable, and REQ-159/REQ-160 (which will write the actual code) are the right point to tighten the @spec if narrower typing is possible then.
four_questions.scope_creep: None found. The design creates no module, adds no dependency, and explicitly defers non-numeric marshalling to REQ-159/REQ-160 rather than pre-building generic plumbing for cases OQ-6 didn't ask it to settle. §4's WASM-12 parity binding restates what decision 0014 already commits to ('WASM-12 defines the WASM host API by parity with Lua's') rather than inventing new scope.

result.anti_patterns_check: No violation found. Notably the design's §1 empirical findings are real runs against the adopted tv-labs/lua runtime and a real Postgres jsonb column, not inferred from documentation or inherited from decision 0014's own doc-sourced claims — this is exactly the discipline the 'Inheriting a claim from a record instead of re-deriving it from the source' anti-pattern entry asks for, applied correctly here rather than violated.
result.decision_0014_consistency: Internally consistent. OQ-6 names Letflow.Engine.VariableMerge and JSONB variable storage as the two things the rule must cover centrally 'before LUA-11 is expanded, not rediscovered per host function' -- the design's §3 module (Letflow.Engine.LuaNumberMarshalling) is scoped exactly to that, and correctly references VariableMerge.merge/3's incoming_variables map as the real integration point rather than a placeholder. The design does not claim decision 0014's doc-sourced Elixir-ecosystem facts as verified; it independently re-verifies the number-marshalling-relevant subset (Lua.eval!/2, Lua.set!/3, Jason round-trip, real jsonb column) empirically, which is stronger than what 0014 itself could assert. §4's WASM-12 binding correctly cites 0014's Decision (4) rather than re-deciding it. No contradiction with any S0 decision record was introduced.
result.summary: Design-only artefact, no lib/letflow/engine/ change (confirmed via git diff --stat). All four REVIEWER questions checked; no crutch, no supervision concern (none applicable), no blocking type-safety gap, no scope creep. Internally consistent with decision 0014's OQ-6 framing and correctly cites (rather than re-derives) 0014's WASM-12 parity commitment. Findings in the design are empirically verified, not doc-inherited, which is the strongest form of evidence this project asks for. One non-blocking note: to_lua/1 and from_lua/1's term()->term() signatures are appropriately broad for a design stage; REQ-159/REQ-160 should consider a narrower @spec if the implementation allows it, but this does not block the design gate.
